Thoughtful Design, Built to Last

Formline Architecture Studio creates homes, workplaces and public spaces rooted in honest materials, careful light, and a deep respect for the people who use them. From first sketch to final walkthrough, we design buildings meant to be lived in for generations.

View Our Projects Start a Conversation

Signature Projects

A glimpse at the work that defines our approach — quiet, considered, and responsive to site and client alike.

Birchwood Residence

A family home on a sloped lot, organized around a central courtyard that frames views of the surrounding fir forest.

See the project

Alder Street Studios

An adaptive reuse of a 1920s warehouse into light-filled creative offices for a growing design collective.

See the project

Cedar Park Library

A small civic building designed to feel generous: a reading hall with a folded timber ceiling and garden views.

See the project

Our Approach

We believe good architecture begins with listening — to the client, to the site, and to the climate. Every project at Formline starts with questions before answers, and every design decision is tested against how it will feel to actually inhabit the space.

We work in small, dedicated teams so that every project receives the full attention of a senior architect from concept through construction, not a handoff between departments.

Meet the Team

Have a Site in Mind?

Whether you're planning a new home, a renovation, or a commercial space, we'd love to hear about it. Reach out and let's talk through your ideas.

Projects

From quiet family homes to civic landmarks, every Formline project begins with a question: how should this place feel to the people who use it? Below is a selection of completed and ongoing work spanning residential, cultural, and commercial typologies across the Pacific Northwest.

  • Residential
  • Cultural
  • Commercial
  • Adaptive Reuse
  • Public Space

Selected Work

Hollow Pine Residence

Sisters, OR · 2023

A single-family retreat organized around a central courtyard, using salvaged timber and deep roof overhangs to mediate high-desert sun and snow.

Elmhurst Branch Library

Portland, OR · 2022

A 12,000 sq ft public library replacing a 1960s structure, with a reading hall lit entirely by north-facing clerestory windows.

Foundry Lofts

Tacoma, WA · 2021

Adaptive reuse of a 1910s iron foundry into twenty-two live-work units, preserving the original crane rail and brick facade.

Driftline House

Cannon Beach, OR · 2020

A weekend home cantilevered toward the shoreline, built to withstand coastal wind loads while staying visually light.

Cedar Grove Community Center

Eugene, OR · In progress

A multi-use gathering hall for a rural district, designed with prefabricated glulam trusses to shorten construction time.

Alder Street Studio Shops

Portland, OR · 2019

Three ground-floor retail spaces with folding glass storefronts, designed to open fully onto the sidewalk in warmer months.

Featured Project

Marrow Street Pavilion

Portland, OR · Completed 2023 · 4,800 sq ft

Commissioned by the city as a flexible event and market space, the Marrow Street Pavilion sits at the edge of a redeveloped industrial lot in the Central Eastside. The brief called for a structure that could host a farmers market on Saturday mornings and a jazz performance the same evening, with no fixed seating and minimal mechanical systems.

Our response was a folded timber roof supported on eight exposed steel columns, open on all sides but deep enough to shelter the plaza from Portland's frequent drizzle. Operable canvas screens let the space close down in winter without sealing it off entirely. The project was delivered on a municipal budget of $1.1M and completed four weeks ahead of schedule.

Since opening, the pavilion has hosted over sixty public events and became the anchor for the surrounding neighborhood's annual lantern festival.

Our Team

At Formline, architecture is a collaborative craft. Our team brings together architects, interior designers and project managers who share a belief that thoughtful design should be both beautiful and built to last. We work in small, dedicated teams so every client has direct access to the people shaping their project — from first sketch to final walkthrough.

Founded in 2011, the studio has grown from a two-person practice to a team of twelve, but we've kept the same values: listen carefully, design rigorously, and build relationships that outlast the ribbon-cutting.

How We Work Together

Studio Reviews

Every project is reviewed by the whole studio at key milestones, so each design benefits from multiple perspectives.

One Point of Contact

Clients work with a lead architect throughout the project — no hand-offs, no confusion about who to call.

Continuous Learning

We dedicate time each month to research, materials testing and site visits to keep our craft sharp.

Meet the Team

Elena Marsh

Founding Principal, AIA

With over twenty years of practice, Elena leads the studio's design direction and oversees every project from concept through completion. She holds a Master of Architecture from the University of Oregon.

David Okafor

Senior Architect

David specializes in adaptive reuse and historic renovation, balancing preservation with modern function. He joined Formline in 2015 after practicing in Chicago.

Priya Nathan

Interior Design Lead

Priya ensures the interiors of every Formline project feel as considered as the architecture itself, from material palettes to custom millwork.

Marcus Lindqvist

Project Architect

Marcus manages the day-to-day coordination of our residential projects, keeping schedules, budgets and craftsmanship in balance.

Sofia Reyes

Sustainability Consultant

Sofia guides energy modeling and material sourcing to help every project meet or exceed Passive House standards where feasible.

Jon Fairweather

Studio Manager

Jon keeps the studio running smoothly, from client scheduling to permit coordination, so our architects can focus on design.

Interested in Joining Formline?

We're always glad to hear from thoughtful architects and designers who share our values. Send your portfolio and a short note to our studio.

Services

Formline Architecture Studio offers a full spectrum of architectural services, from first sketch to final walkthrough. Whether you're planning a new home, a commercial build-out, or a sensitive renovation, we tailor our process and fees to the scale and ambitions of your project. Below is an overview of what we offer, typical starting investment, and how a project unfolds when you work with us.

What We Offer

Residential Design

Custom single-family homes and additions designed around how you actually live, from compact infill lots to sprawling rural sites.

Starting at $18,000

Commercial & Workplace Design

Offices, retail spaces, and mixed-use buildings that balance brand identity, code compliance, and day-to-day usability.

Starting at $35,000

Interior Architecture

Space planning, material palettes, and built-in detailing for interiors that need to feel considered down to the hardware.

Starting at $9,500

Renovation & Adaptive Reuse

Sensitive upgrades to existing structures, including historic buildings, that respect original character while meeting modern needs.

Starting at $14,000

Sustainability Consulting

Passive design strategies, material sourcing, and energy modeling to reduce long-term operating costs and environmental impact.

Starting at $4,500

Urban & Site Planning

Master planning, zoning strategy, and feasibility studies for developers and institutions working on multi-building sites.

Starting at $22,000

Pricing above reflects typical starting fees for a defined scope of work in the Portland metro area. Every proposal is scoped individually after an initial consultation — see contact to request a quote.

Our Process

Most projects move through six stages, though timelines flex depending on scope, permitting jurisdiction, and site conditions.

  1. 1

    Initial Consultation

    We meet on-site or by video to understand your goals, budget, and constraints, and outline a scope and fee proposal.

  2. 2

    Concept Design

    We develop initial massing, floor plans, and visual studies to explore the project's core ideas before committing to details.

  3. 3

    Design Development

    Approved concepts are refined into detailed drawings, material selections, and structural and mechanical coordination.

  4. 4

    Permitting & Documentation

    We prepare construction documents and manage submission and review with local permitting authorities on your behalf.

  5. 5

    Construction Administration

    We work alongside your contractor, answering field questions and reviewing progress to keep the build true to the design.

  6. 6

    Project Completion

    A final walkthrough confirms every detail meets expectations, followed by close-out documentation and warranty support.
